summary: H.J. Res. 210 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and revoke an Environmental Protection Agency decision. Specifically, it voids the EPA's authorization that allowed the California Air Resources Board to amend its regulations on emissions from ocean-going vessels while docked at berth.

affected_groups.effect: Loses the authorization granted by the EPA to amend and enforce its expanded ocean-going vessels at-berth emissions regulation.
No longer required by the authorized California amendment to meet the expanded auxiliary engine emissions reductions requirements while at berth.

key_provisions: Expresses congressional disapproval of the EPA rule titled California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision.
States that the disapproved rule shall have no force or effect.
Revokes the authorization given to the California Air Resources Board to amend its Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth Regulation.
missing_information: Specific economic costs or savings associated with the disapproval of the rule.
Exact details on which new categories of vessels were originally included in the California amendment.
The broader environmental impact on air quality.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.J. Res. 210 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and revoke an Environmental Protection Agency decision. Specifically, it voids the EPA's authorization that allowed the California Air Resources Board to amend its regulations on emissions from ocean-going vessels while docked at berth.
summary_detail.significance: The resolution halts a specific state-level environmental regulation approved by the EPA regarding vessel emissions. It affects the regulatory authority of California to enforce expanded emission reduction rules on ships docked at its ports.
